facts.text: Shorter began as Cross Keys, named for an early settler’s South Carolina birthplace, before being renamed after Governor John Gill Shorter.
Before 1832, the land that is now Shorter was part of Creek Indian Territory, and the area was incorporated into Macon County after the Creek removal.
Shorter hosts one of the longest stretches of the Old Federal Road, built in 1804, a historic route through Alabama.
The town’s center sits on a low ridge that drains south to Cubahatchee Creek and north to Calebee Creek, both feeding the Tallapoosa River.
Shorter officially incorporated on February 29, 1984, after more than a century of community life.
The town embodies memories of the Creek Indian Nation, the Old South, and the Civil Rights Movement, reflecting its layered history.
